newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia aims for more bank ownership transfers.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia aims for more bank ownership transfers.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) is looking at further transfers of ownership in the banking sector, NBS Vice-governor Jozef Mudrik told the economic weekly Trend in an interview.

"We cannot, and neither are we aiming to, slow down ownership transformation in the banking sphere," he said adding: "But the Czech Republic's experience confirm the importance of transparency in ownership."
He did not elaborate on what steps the central bank was taking.

Several Czech banks have recently experienced problems, blamed in part on weak securities legislation which has allowed secretive investment groups to take stakes in banks, and their opaque dealings have hurt confidence in the sector.

Last week, the NBS rejected a request made by steel maker VSZ to increase its holdings in IRB, the third largest commercial bank, to over 20 percent, due to a lack of plan on participation in restructuring process in the bank.
NBS also requested VSZ and it's alleged securities trader, ARDS a.s., to lower within a month their joint share in IRB to below the legal 15 percent limit of the bank's basic capital.
But VSZ officials said there were ways for the firm to attain its goals even if did not have the central bank's blessing through some of its 100 subsidiaries.
Mudrik said that while a certain concentration of capital and strengthening in banks was needed, it would have to be done trensparently and by a solvent investor.
